page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz. It features 40 virtual CPUs derived from 20 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.8 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. The underlying virtualization is managed via the KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark results place the ecs.hfg6.10xlarge consistently in the average performance tier. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1438.99 and a multi-core score of 38378.07, supported by a Passmark CPU score of 34691.95. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 2133.36 GB/sec, which drops to 108.89 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Cryptographic and vector operations are accelerated by hardware flags including AVX, AVX-512, and AES.

With its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, this instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and database operations. It handles Redis SET operations at a rate of 34.78 million operations per second and static web serving at 25.35 GB/sec. However, the lack of local storage and dedicated GPU accelerators limits its efficiency for large-scale deep learning training or high-I/O local database tasks. Qualitatively, it offers a stable, predictable resource profile for enterprise applications requiring dedicated CPU execution without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated tiers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is a general-purpose, KVM-virtualized server instance configured with 40 dedicated vCPUs and 192.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz, it features 20 physical cores with hyper-threading and supports AVX-512 and AES instruction sets. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations place its performance in the average tier, with a Passmark CPU score of 34691.95 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 38378.07. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, web serving, and database operations like Redis, where it achieves 34.78 million SET operations per second. It offers a balanced, dedicated compute profile without the overhead of specialized hardware.
